proof_review: Finite-order Euclidean isometries fix an averaged orbit point. After conjugating that point into the bounded simplex alcove, its stabilizer is generated by a proper subset of the walls, hence lies in a maximal standard parabolic. Normality transfers the avoidance hypothesis. No finite-index assumption enters.

For g in a torsion-free normal subgroup, g s_i g^-1 s_i lies in that subgroup. Two nonparallel Euclidean hyperplanes intersect. The product of their distinct reflections fixes the intersection, so is a nonidentity finite-order element in a discrete point stabilizer. This rules out every nonparallel image wall.

Orthogonality gives a sign on every preserved wall-normal line. Nonzero pairwise inner products propagate the sign along the connected affine diagram; spanning normals then give plus or minus the identity. The negative choice is a point inversion of order two. In dimension one the two possible linear parts give the same conclusion directly.

The actual universal spherical residue hypothesis, together with the acquired regular residue action, equates the finite orders of W_i and its image. This proves local injection. The N-orbits of cosets are exactly quotient cosets and existential incidence lifts by normality; reconstruction is used only for an already existing regular hypertope.

The conclusion is necessary, not sufficient, for a translation quotient to be a hypertope. Product avoidance and actual flag transitivity remain independent requirements. Period-lattice exhaustion is neither asserted nor certified.
